                                       ARTICLE 7.
                                 TAXES AND ASSESSMENTS

         7.1.     Obligation to Pay Taxes and Assessments. Prior to the Commencement Date and
on the first day of each calendar month of the Term, Lessee shall pay as Additional Rent to Lessor
an amount equal to the greater of (a) 1/12th of the most recently ascertainable real estate annual tax
bill(s), or (b) if applicable, the amount required under the Master Lease for real estate and other
impositions (“Taxes and Assessments”). Notwithstanding the foregoing, Lessee shall fund any
initial escrow deposits due to Owner on the Commencement Date.

        7.2.    Application of Deposits. Provided that Lessee makes the monthly deposits of Taxes
and Assessments when and as due, Lessor shall pay the Taxes and Assessments, or cause the same
to be paid, when and as due, before any fine, penalty, interest or cost may be added thereto for the
nonpayment thereof and Lessee shall not be responsible for any such fine, penalty, interest or cost
imposed or levied as a result of Lessor’s failure to do so. If the total of the monthly payments as
made under this Article shall be insufficient to pay the Taxes and Assessments when due, then
Lessee shall on demand pay Lessor the amount necessary to make up the deficiency and the
monthly deposits shall be adjusted per Section 7.1. If the total of the monthly payments made by
Lessee under Section 7.1 shall exceed the amount necessary to pay any Taxes and Assessments
when due, then Lessor shall apply any such excess remaining after such payment to the next
monthly payments that are due and Lessee shall receive a credit against the next monthly payments
that are due under Section 7.1 up to the amount of the excess applied to such payments, and the
monthly deposits shall be adjusted per Section 7.1. In the event of termination of the Lease or the
curing of any Event of Default, Lessor shall provide Lessee with an accounting of any and all
deposits made and payments applied. Upon termination of this Lease or the curing of an Event of
Default, as applicable, the excess of any deposits made over proper payments made from said
deposits shall be repaid to Lessee, and any deficiency shall be paid to Lessor.

        7.3.    Tax Contest. Lessee may, at Lessee’s sole cost and expense, bring a tax contest to
affect a reduction of Taxes and Assessments and Lessor, at Lessee’s expense, shall cooperate with
Lessee in such contest. Lessor shall have the right to join such proceeding initiated by Lessee.
Lessee shall reimburse Lessor for Lessor’s direct costs of cooperating or joining with Lessee in
such contest. If Lessee elects not to contest Taxes and Assessments, Lessor shall have the right to
do so in its own name and at its sole cost and expense. If any refund shall be due from any taxing
authority in respect of any Taxes and Assessments paid by Lessee, the same shall be paid over to
or retained by Lessee for the period during the Term.

        7.4.   Notice from Lessor. Upon Lessee’s request, Lessor shall promptly deliver to Lessee
copies of any and all notices of assessments, valuations for purposes of assessments, invoices, bills
or other notices regarding Taxes and Assessments which it may from time to time receive relating
to the Leased Property or any part thereof, provided, however, that Lessor’s failure to do so shall
not be a default hereunder by Lessor and shall in no way diminish Lessee’s obligation hereunder
to make monthly deposits of such Taxes and Assessments.

        7.5.  Proration. Any Taxes and Assessments relating to a fiscal period of any authority,
a part of which is included within the Term and a part of which is included in a period of time


                                              7

===== PAGE 412 =====
before or after the Term, shall be adjusted pro rata between Lessor and Lessee and each party shall
be responsible for its pro rata share of any such Taxes and Assessments.

                                           ARTICLE 8.
                                          OCCUPANCY

        8.1.    Permitted Use. During the Term, the Leased Property shall be used and occupied
by Lessee for and as a skilled nursing facility with not less than the number of licensed beds set
forth in Schedule 1 of this Lease and in connection therewith the provision of food, recreational,
rehabilitative and therapy services, and such other uses as may be necessary or incidental thereto
(its “Permitted Use”), and for no other purpose. Subject to the terms of Article 14 hereof, Lessee
(or Lessee’s permitted Affiliate, assignee or subtenant, as appropriate) shall at all times during the
Term maintain in good standing and full force probationary or non-probationary licenses issued
by the State Health Department and any other Governmental Agencies permitting the operation on
the Leased Property of a skilled nursing facility with the same number of skilled nursing beds as
set forth in Schedule 1 of this Lease and maintain in good standing and full force provider
agreements pursuant to which the Facility shall be entitled to participate in the Medicare and
Medicaid reimbursement programs and receive reimbursement from the State Health Department,
CMS or any other government program for services provided at the Facility.

        8.2.    Standards of Operation. During the Term, Lessee shall continuously operate the
Leased Property consistent with industry standards for similar nursing facilities in a similar
location, including, the following:

             (a)     to operate the Facility in a prudent manner and in compliance with
Applicable Laws and regulations relating thereto;

               (b)     to maintain sufficient personal property, equipment and inventories of types
and quantities at the Facility to enable Lessee to adequately perform operation of the Facility;

              (c)     subject to and in accordance with Section 4.1, to keep all improvements,
personal property and equipment located on or used or useful in connection with the Facility in
good repair, working order and condition, reasonable wear and tear excepted, and from time to
time make all needed and proper repairs, replacements, additions and improvements thereto to
keep the same in good operating condition;

               (d)  to pay all trade payables, salaries and other operating expenses as they
become due and to operate the Leased Property as a facility substantially similar or better than as
operated on the Commencement Date;

               (e)      to operate and use the Leased Property with all required licenses and permits
for such operation, if any;

              (f)    to provide prompt written notice to Lessor of material adverse or
extraordinary developments, lawsuits, administrative hearings, violation of any Legal
Requirements and fines relating to the use and operation of the Facility; and



                                              8

===== PAGE 413 =====
               (g)     subject to medical and nursing decision-making and to applicable law
including, but not limited to, laws with respect to resident choice and provided such use will not
have a material adverse financial or operational impact on the Facility, to use preferred service
providers as directed by Lessor.

        8.3.    Standards, Not Control. Lessor and Lessee acknowledge and agree that Lessee is
obligated to undertake such actions as are reasonably necessary to properly achieve the standard
of operation for the Facility as set forth herein, and that, although Lessor shall have the right to
undertake all enforcement rights as provided herein, in the event that a required standard of
operation is not maintained by Lessee, the means and methods used and actions taken to operate
the Facility are within the sole control and election of Lessee, and are not specified by or under
the control of Lessor. Accordingly, Lessor shall have no responsibility for any action taken by
Lessee in order to manage or operate the Facility in accordance with the standards set forth herein.

       8.4.    Delays. Lessee acknowledges that Lessee’s failure or repeated delays in making
prompt payment in accordance with the terms of any agreement, leases, invoices or statements for
purchase or lease of personal property, equipment and supplies will be detrimental to the reputation
of Lessor, Lessee and the Facility. Accordingly, Lessee agrees that Lessee shall make all
reasonable efforts to pay when due all undisputed amounts owed by Lessee in connection with the
operation of the Facility.

        8.5.    At all times during the Term of the Lease, Zev Schwartz shall beneficially own,
directly or indirectly, as a beneficiary of trusts or otherwise, one hundred percent (100%) of Lessee
in the aggregate and shall be the controlling manager of each Lessee.

       8.6.    Intentionally Omitted.

         8.7.    Additional Indebtedness. Lessee hereby covenants and agrees that during the Term
it shall not, except for liabilities incurred in the ordinary course of business or in connection with
a working capital loan, create, incur, assume or guarantee, or permit to exist or become or remain
liable directly or indirectly upon, any Indebtedness except Indebtedness of Lessee to Lessor.

       8.8.     Residency Agreements. Lessee shall comply in all material respects with the terms
and provisions of each agreement and undertaking entered into with or provided to the residents
of the Facility (“Residency Agreements”), including all undertakings and representations
regarding the use, condition and operation of the Facility and services to be provided to the
residents. In the event this Lease is terminated and Lessee is no longer in possession of the Leased
Property, all Residency Agreements shall be assigned by Lessee to Lessor or Lessor’s designee.

        8.9.    Nuisance or Waste. Lessee will not suffer any act to be done or any condition to
exist on the Leased Property which may be dangerous or which may, in law, constitute a public or
private nuisance or which may void or make voidable any insurance policy then in force on the
Leased Property. Lessee shall, at its sole cost, comply with all Insurance Requirements. Lessee
shall not use or suffer or permit the use of the Leased Property, if any, for any unlawful purpose.
Lessee shall not commit or suffer to be committed any waste on the Leased Property, or in the
Facility, nor shall Lessee cause or permit any unlawful nuisance thereon or therein. Lessee shall
not suffer nor permit the Leased Property, or any portion thereof, to be used in such a manner as


                                              9

===== PAGE 414 =====
(i) might reasonably impair Lessor’s title thereto or to any portion thereof, or (ii) might reasonably
allow a claim for adverse possession.

        8.10. Reduction in Number of Licensed Beds. Lessee shall, within ten (10) days
following its receipt thereof, provide Lessor with a copy of any notice from the State Health
Departments or any federal, state or municipal governmental agency or authority regarding any
reduction in the number of licensed beds and pursuant to Section 14.3, Lessor shall have the right
to contest, by appropriate legal or administrative proceedings, any such reduction.

        8.11. Environmental Laws. During the Term, Lessee shall only use the Leased Property
in accordance with Environmental Laws (as hereinafter defined) and shall not use nor permit the
Leased Property to be used for the treatment, storage or disposal of any Hazardous Substances (as
defined below) nor for any purpose involving the use of the Hazardous Substances; provided,
however, that Lessee may use in and store at the Facility such materials and substances as are
customarily used in nursing facilities in the state in which the Leased Property is located, but only
in such quantities as are reasonably necessary for the routine business operation of the Facility.
Lessee hereby agrees to indemnify, defend and hold Lessor harmless from and against, and shall
reimburse Lessor for, any loss, claim, liability, damages, injunctive relief, injuries to persons,
property or natural resources, costs, expense, action and causes of action in connection with the
use, generation, treatment, storage, release or disposal of Hazardous Substances by Lessee at or
from the Real Property during the Term hereof, including the cost of any required or necessary
repair, cleanup or detoxification and the preparation of any closure or other required work to be
performed, to the full extent that such action is attributable, directly or indirectly, to the use,
generation, treatment, storage, release or disposal of Hazardous Substances by Lessee on the Real
Property during the Term hereof.

        8.12. Management Fees. Lessee hereby covenants and agrees that any management fees
paid for the management of the Facility during the Term shall not exceed six percent (6%) of its
gross revenues.

        8.13. Return of Leased Property Upon Termination. Upon expiration or termination of
this Lease for any reason, Lessee will return the Leased Property to Lessor in the condition required
under the Master Lease, with the same number and type of nursing beds with respect to the Facility
set forth in Schedule 1 of this Lease and with an unrestricted license in full force and good standing
for no less than the same number and type of nursing beds with respect to the Facility set forth in
Schedule 1 of this Lease. No reduction in the number of licensed beds shall entitle Lessee to any
reduction or adjustment of the Rent payable hereunder, which shall be and continue to be payable
by Lessee in the full amount set forth herein.

        8.14. Survival. The provisions of this Article 8 shall survive the expiration or sooner
termination of this Lease to the extent of any ongoing effects on Lessor or its successors with
respect to a breach during the Term by Lessee of its obligations under this Article.

                                           ARTICLE 9.
                                          INSURANCE

        9.1.    Property Insurance. Subject to any additional requirements contained in the Master
Lease and which are reasonable and consistent with industry standards, Lessee shall, at its sole
cost and expense, during the Term of this Lease maintain fire and casualty and other hazards
insurance as now or subsequently maybe be covered by an “all-risk” policy, with coverage for
earthquake in amounts and in forms satisfactory to Lessor, and with extended coverage and such
other endorsements as Lessor may from time to time reasonably require, on the Leased Property.
Such insurance shall, at all times, be maintained in an amount equal to the full replacement value
of the Leased Property, but not less than that reasonably required by Owner pursuant to industry
standards. Such insurance shall at all times be payable to Owner, Lessor and Lessee, as their
interests may appear and shall contain a loss payable clause to the holder of any Mortgage, as its
interest may appear. The amount of such property insurance shall be not less than 100% of the full
replacement cost of the Leased Property, and owned by Lessor from time to time, without reduction
for depreciation. The determination of the replacement cost amount shall be adjusted annually to
comply with the requirements of the insurer issuing such coverage. Full replacement cost, as used
herein, means, with respect to the Leased Property, the cost of replacing the Leased Property
without regard to deduction for depreciation, exclusive of the cost of excavations, foundations and
footings below the lowest basement floor, and means, with respect to such furniture, furnishings,
fixtures, equipment and other items, the cost of replacing the same. Each such policy or policies
of property insurance shall contain the following provisions, all subject to Lessor approval in form
and content: (A) a replacement cost endorsement; (B) either an agreed amount endorsement (to
waive the operation of any coinsurance provisions) or a waiver of any co-insurance provisions;
(C) law and ordinance coverage in an amount satisfactory to Lessor; and (D) coverage for
interruption in utility services.

        9.2.    Liability Insurance. Lessee shall also, at Lessee’s sole cost and expense, cause to
be issued and shall maintain at all times during the Term and at any other time Lessee shall be in
possession of the Leased Property, “occurrence” based insurance in accordance with the
requirements set forth in the Master Lease and which are reasonable and consistent with industry
standards, covering Lessor against claims for bodily injury, or property damage occurring upon,
in or about the Leased Property, or in or upon the adjoining streets, sidewalks, passageways and
areas, such insurance to afford protection to the limits reasonably established by Lessee in the
operation of its business, but not less than One Million Dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence and
Three Million Dollars ($3,000,000) in the aggregate or any greater amount required by the Master
Lease and which are reasonable and consistent with industry standards, adding Lessor and Owner
as additional insureds and loss payees, as appropriate. Each such policy or policies of liability
insurance shall (A) provide coverage for claims for personal injury, advertising injury, bodily
injury, death and property damage liability with respect to the Facility and operations related
thereto, whether on or off the Leased Property; (B) include broad form contractual liability
coverage including coverage for the indemnities contained herein.

       9.3.    Other Insurance. Lessee shall also, at Lessee’s sole cost and expense, cause to be
issued and shall maintain at all times during the Term and while Lessee shall be in possession of
the Leased Property, insurance in accordance with the requirements set forth in any the Master


                                            11

===== PAGE 416 =====
Lease and which are reasonable and consistent with industry standards, but in no event with
coverage less than:

                (a)      Broad form boiler and machinery insurance covering the major components
of the central heating, air conditioning and ventilating systems, boilers, other pressure vessels, high
pressure piping and machinery, elevators and escalators, if any, and other similar equipment
installed in the Leased Property, in an amount equal to 100% of the full replacement cost of the
Leased Property. Such policy or policies shall insure against physical damage to and loss of
occupancy and use of the Leased Property arising out of an accident or breakdown covered under
such policy or policies and shall include all of the following coverage: (A) business interruption
including rental value, (B) extra expense, (C) consequential damage and (D) interruption in utility
services power supply.

                (b)      Professional liability and malpractice insurance with limits of at least
$1,000,000 per occurrence (claim)/$3,000,000 in the aggregate, and covering acts occurring prior
to the date hereof. Each Lessee shall cause, each physician or nurse practitioner with clinical
privileges at the Facility to carry professional liability and malpractice insurance with limits of not
less than $1,000,000 per occurrence (claim)/$3,000,000 in the aggregate. Lessor retains the right
to periodically review the amount of such liability insurance and to require an increase in the
amount of the same should Lessor deem an increase to be reasonably prudent under the existing
circumstances.

                (c)     Lessee shall at all times keep in effect business interruption insurance with
loss of rents endorsement naming Lessor as an insured in an amount equal to twelve (12) months
of Base Rent plus scheduled Additional Rent (e.g., insurance, taxes). All proceeds of any business
interruption insurance or loss of rents coverage shall be applied, first, to the payment of any Base
Rent payments for the next succeeding twelve (12) months to the extent that such payments are
due and owing; second, to the payment of any real estate and personal property taxes and insurance
deposits required for the next succeeding twelve (12) months to the extent that such payments are
due and owing; and, thereafter, after all necessary repairing, rebuilding, restoring or replacing has
been completed as required by this Lease and the Master Lease, any remaining balance of such
proceeds shall be paid to Lessee. Each such policy or policies shall contain the following
provisions, all subject to Lessor's approval in form and content: (i) either an agreed amount
endorsement (to waive the operation of any co-insurance provisions) or a waiver of any co-
insurance provisions; (ii) law and ordinance coverage in an amount satisfactory to Lessor; (iii) an
extended period of indemnity endorsement providing that after the repair of any physical loss to
the Leased Property, the continued loss of income will be insured until the earlier of the time that
(a) such income returns to the same level as it was at prior to the date on which the physical loss
occurred or (b) twelve (12) months from the date that the Leased Property is repaired or replaced
and operations are resumed in the manner that such operations were conducted prior to the date of
the physical loss to the Leased Property giving rise to such insurance obligation, which payments
shall be made notwithstanding the expiration of the policy prior to the end of such period. All
proceeds of any business interruption insurance or loss of rents coverage shall be applied, first, to
the payment of any Base Rent payment, taxes and assessments and insurance premiums or deposits
required for the next succeeding twelve (12) months to the extent that such payments are due and
owing and, thereafter, after all necessary repairing, rebuilding, restoring or replacing has been


                                              12

===== PAGE 417 =====
completed as required by the pertinent Articles of this Lease, any remaining balance of such
proceeds shall be paid over to the Lessee.

               (d)      During the period of any construction on the Leased Property or renovation
or alteration of the Leased Property, a so-called "Builder's All-Risk Completed Value" or
"Course of Construction" insurance policy in non-reporting form for any improvements under
construction, including for demolition and increased cost of construction or renovation, in an
amount equal to 100% of the estimated replacement cost on the date of completion, including "soft
cost" coverage, and workers' compensation and employers liability insurance covering all persons
engaged in such construction, in an amount at least equal to the minimum required by law. In
addition, each contractor and subcontractor shall be required to provide Lessor with a certificate
of insurance for (i) workers' compensation and employers liability insurance covering all persons
engaged by such contractor or subcontractor in such construction in an amount at least equal to the
minimum required by law, and (ii) general liability insurance showing minimum limits of at least
$3,000,000, including coverage for premises/operations and products and completed operations.
Each contractor and subcontractor also shall cover Lessor as additional insured under such liability
policy and shall defend, indemnify and hold Lessor harmless from and against any and all claims,
damages, liabilities, costs and expenses arising out of, relating to or otherwise in connection with
the performance by each contractor and subcontractor of such construction.

               (e)   If the Leased Property or any part thereof is identified by the Secretary of
Housing and Urban Development as being situated in an area now or subsequently designated as
having special flood hazards (including those areas designated as Zone A or Zone V), flood
insurance in an amount equal to 100% of the lesser of the (A) replacement value of the Leased
Property or (B) maximum amount of flood insurance available.

                (f)    Motor vehicle (auto) liability coverage for all owned hired and non-owned
automobiles, including rented and leased automobiles, containing minimum limits per occurrence
of greater of $1,000,000 or at such amounts as are in force as of the date hereof.

                (g)    With respect to the Leased Property, insurance for certified and uncertified
acts of terrorism insurance in such amounts as are required by Lessor.

                (h)     Crime coverage providing blanket employee dishonesty insurance with
limits of not less than $500,000.

               (i)      Worker’s compensation insurance or other similar insurance which may be
required by governmental authorities or applicable legal requirements in an amount not less than
the minimum required by law. Lessee may self-insure for worker’s compensation, provided that
such self-insurance is at all times maintained in full compliance with the laws of the State of Rhode
Island.

       9.4.    General Insurance Requirements. All policies of insurance shall provide, to the
extent not otherwise required by the Master Lease (such requirements being reasonable and
consistent with industry standards):




                                             13

===== PAGE 418 =====
               (a)     They are carried in favor of Lessor, Lessee, and Owner, as their respective
interests may appear, and any loss shall be payable as therein provided, notwithstanding any act or
negligence of Lessor or Lessee, which might otherwise result in forfeiture of insurance;

                (b)      They shall not be canceled, terminated, reduced or materially modified
without at least thirty (30) days’ prior written notice to Lessor and Owner;

               (c)     Be issued by companies approved by Lessor and licensed to do business in
the state where the Leased Property is located, with a claims paying ability rating of "A" or better
by A.M. Best Company;

                (d)     Contain the complete address of the Leased Property (or a complete legal
description);

                (e)     Be for a term of at least one year;

                (f)     Contain deductibles no greater than $10,000 or as otherwise required by
Lessor;

               (g)     Be subject to the approval of Lessor as to insurance companies, amounts,
content, forms of policies, method by which premiums are paid and expiration dates;

                (h)      All policies required under this Lease will contain: (i) a provision that such
policies shall not be canceled or amended, including any amendment that would reduce the scope
or limits of coverage or remove any endorsement to such policy or cause the same to no longer be
in full force and effect, or failed to be renewed, without at least thirty (30) days prior written notice
to Lessor in each instance; and (ii) a waiver of all rights of subrogation against Lessor; and

                (i)    A standard mortgagee clause in favor of any mortgagee, and shall contain,
if obtainable, a waiver of the insurer’s right of subrogation against funds paid under the standard
mortgagee endorsement which are to be used to pay the cost of any repairing, rebuilding, restoring
or replacing.

        9.5.    Payment of Premiums. Lessee shall deliver to Lessor evidence satisfactory to
Lessor in its discretion that such insurance policies have been paid current as of the date hereof.
Lessee shall deliver to Lessor certified copies of any such insurance policies promptly upon
request. No premiums for any policies or policies of insurance required under this Lease or
otherwise held with respect to the Leased Property, whether by Lessee or any other person, shall
be paid by Lessee or by any other person through or by means of any financing arrangement with
any third party lender.

        9.6.   Certificates of Insurance. Certificates of insurance policies required by this Lease
shall be delivered to Lessor and Owner prior to or on the Commencement Date and again thirty
(30) days prior to the anniversary date of the Lease covering the next Lease year. Upon receipt
thereof, Lessee shall deliver copies of the actual policies to Lessor, which certificates and policies
shall be updated annually not less than thirty (30) days prior to the expiration date thereof.

         9.7.   Lessee Covenants. Lessee will not do or omit to do or keep anything in, upon or

personal property or such adjacent areas, or (b) make any such insurance void or voidable or
otherwise invalidate the obligations of the insurer contained therein.

       9.8.    Waiver of Subrogation. Lessor and Lessee agree that with respect to any property
loss which is covered by insurance then being carried by Lessor or Lessee, the party carrying such
insurance and suffering said loss releases the other of and from any and all claims with respect to

subrogation against the other on account thereof.

                                           ARTICLE 11.
                                           CASUALTY

        11.1. Restoration and Repair. If, during the Term, the Leased Property shall be totally or
partially (more than seventy-five percent (75%)) destroyed and thereby rendered Unsuitable for
its Permitted Use, Lessee shall give Lessor prompt notice thereof and either Lessor or Lessee may,
by the giving of notice thereof to the other party within thirty (30) days after such casualty occurs,
terminate this Lease, whereupon Lessor shall be entitled to retain the insurance proceeds payable
on account of such damage and Lessee shall pay to Lessor the amount of any deductible. Lessee
further expressly acknowledges, understands and agrees that in the event that this Lease is
terminated as aforesaid, Lessor may settle any insurance claims and Lessee shall, upon request of
Lessor, cooperate in any such settlement. If during the Term, the Leased Property shall be
destroyed or damaged in whole or in part, but the Leased Property either (i) is not rendered
Unsuitable for its Permitted Use or (ii) is rendered Unsuitable for its Permitted Use but neither
Lessor nor Lessee terminates this Lease in the manner provided above, then, Lessee shall give


                                             16

===== PAGE 421 =====
Lessor prompt notice thereof and Lessee shall, subject to the provisions of Section 11.2 below,
repair, reconstruct and replace the Leased Property, or the portion thereof so destroyed or damaged,
substantially similar value and character thereof existing immediately prior to such occurrence and
in compliance with all Legal Requirements, including any alterations to the Leased Property
required to be made by any Governmental Agencies due to any changes in code or building
regulations (which Lessee acknowledges may increase the replacement value of the Leased
Property which Lessee will then be required to insure, due to any changes in code or building
regulations). Subject to the provisions of Section 11.2 below, all such restoration work shall be
started as promptly as practicable and diligently completed at Lessee’s sole cost and expense.
Lessee shall, however, immediately take such action as is necessary to assure that the Leased
Property (or any portion thereof), does not constitute a nuisance or otherwise present or constitute
a health or safety hazard. Lessee shall have the right to discontinue operating the Leased Property
to the extent reasonably necessary to comply with Applicable Laws, or to safely repair, reconstruct
or replace the Leased Property or such portion so destroyed or damaged in accordance with the
requirements of this Article.

        11.2. Escrow and Disbursement of Insurance Proceeds. If this Lease is not otherwise
terminated pursuant to Section 11.1, then in the event of a casualty resulting in a loss to the Leased
Property in excess of Fifty Thousand Dollars ($50,000), the proceeds of all casualty insurance
policies maintained by Lessee shall be deposited in Lessor’s name in an escrow account at a bank
or other financial institution designated by Lessor, and shall be used by Lessee for the repair,
reconstruction or restoration of the Leased Property to its original condition. Lessee shall, at the
time of establishment of such escrow account and from time to time thereafter until said work shall
have been completed and paid for, furnish Lessor with adequate evidence reasonably acceptable
to Lessor that at all times the undisbursed portion of the escrowed insurance proceeds, together
with any funds made available by Lessee, is sufficient to pay for the repair, reconstruction or
restoration in its entirety. Lessor may, at its option, require, prior to advancement of said escrowed
insurance proceeds (i) approve of plans and specifications by an architect or other design
professional appropriate under the circumstances and approved by Lessor and Lessee (which
approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed), (ii) general contractors’ estimates, (iii)
architect’s certificates, (iv) unconditional lien waivers of general contractors, if available, (v)
evidence of approval by all Governmental Agencies and other regulatory bodies whose approval
is required, and (vi) such other terms as set forth in the Master Lease and which are consistent
with industry standards. The escrowed insurance proceeds shall be disbursed by Lessor, not more
than monthly, upon (a) certification of the architect or engineer selected by Lessor and having
supervision of the work that such amounts are the amounts paid or payable for the repair,
reconstruction or restoration and (b) submittal by Lessee of a written requisition and substantiation
therefor on AIA Forms G702 and G703 (or on such other form or forms as may be reasonably
acceptable to Lessor). Lessee shall obtain, and make available to Lessor, receipted bills and, upon
completion of said work, full and final waivers of lien. In the event of a casualty resulting in a
loss payment for the Leased Property in an amount equal to or less than the amount stated above,
the proceeds shall be paid to Lessee, and shall be applied towards repair, reconstruction and
restoration. Any and all loss adjustments with respect to losses payable hereunder shall require
the prior written consent of Lessor, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or
delayed. All salvage resulting from any risk covered by insurance shall belong to Lessee, provided
any rights to the same have been waived by the insurer. In addition, notwithstanding anything in
this Lease to the contrary, Lessee shall be strictly liable and solely responsible for the amount of

                                             17

===== PAGE 422 =====
any deductible and shall pay for all repairs, reconstruction or alterations up to the full amount of
such deductible (and provide evidence of such payment to Lessor by documentation reasonably
acceptable to Lessor) before any insurance proceeds are used for repairs, reconstruction or
alterations. Lessor’s obligations to disburse any insurance proceeds shall be subject to (x) the
collection thereof, and (y) the release of such proceeds by the Owner.

       11.3. No Abatement of Rent. Unless terminated in accordance with the provisions of
Section 11.1 above, this Lease shall remain in full force and effect and Lessee’s obligation to make
all payments of Rent and to pay all Additional Rent as and when required under this Lease shall
remain unabated during the Term notwithstanding any casualty to the Leased Property.

        11.4. Lessee’s Property and Business Interruption Insurance. All insurance proceeds
payable by reason of any loss of or damage to any of Lessee’s Personal Property and the business
interruption insurance maintained for the benefit of Lessee shall be paid to Lessee; provided,
however, no such payments shall diminish or reduce the insurance payments otherwise payable to
or for the benefit of Lessor hereunder.

        11.5. Restoration of Lessee’s Property. If Lessee is required to restore the Leased
Property as hereinabove provided, Lessee shall either (a) restore all alterations and improvements
made by Lessee and Lessee’s Personal Property, or (b) replace such alterations and improvements
and Lessee’s Personal Property with improvements or items of the same or better quality and utility
in the operation of the Leased Property.

        11.6. Waiver. The provisions of this Article shall be considered an express agreement
governing any event of casualty involving the Leased Property and, to the maximum extent
permitted by law, Lessee hereby waives the application of any local or state statute, law, rule,
regulation or ordinance in effect during the Term which provides for such abatement. Lessee
hereby waives any statutory rights of termination which may arise by reason of any damage or
destruction of the Leased Property and agrees that its rights shall be limited to those set forth in
Section 11.1.

                                         ARTICLE 12.
                                       CONDEMNATION

        12.1. Total Condemnation. If all of the Leased Property shall be taken or condemned for
any public or quasi-public use or purpose, by right of eminent domain or by purchase in lieu
thereof, or if a substantial portion of the Leased Property shall be so taken or condemned (i.e., the
portion or portions remaining is or are not sufficient and suitable, in the reasonable judgment of
Lessee, for the continued operation thereof as required herein, so as to effectively render the Leased
Property Unsuitable for its Permitted Use), then this Lease and the Term hereby granted shall cease
and terminate (without prejudice to Lessor’s and Lessee’s respective rights to an award under
Section 12.3 below), as of the date on which the Condemnor takes possession and all Rent shall
be paid by Lessee to Lessor up to that date or refunded by Lessor to Lessee if Rent has previously
been paid by Lessee beyond that date.

        12.2. Partial Condemnation. If a portion of the Leased Property is taken, and the portion
or portions remaining can, in the reasonable judgment of Lessee, be adapted and used for the


                                             18

===== PAGE 423 =====
conduct of Lessee’s business operation in accordance with the terms of this Lease, such that the
Leased Property is not effectively rendered Unsuitable for its Permitted Use, then the Lessee shall,
utilizing condemnation proceeds paid to Lessor from the Condemnor, promptly restore the
remaining portion or portions thereof to a condition comparable to their condition at the time of
such taking or condemnation, less the portion or portions lost by the taking, and this Lease shall
continue in full force and effect. Lessee shall have the right to discontinue operating the Leased
Property to the extent reasonably necessary to comply with Applicable Laws, or to safely restore
the remaining portion or portions thereof in accordance with the requirements of this Article 12.

        12.3. Disbursement of Award. The entire award for the Leased Property or the portion
or portions thereof so taken shall be apportioned between Lessor and Lessee as follows: (a) if this
Lease terminates due to a taking or condemnation, Lessor shall be entitled to the entire award;
provided, however, that any portion of the award expressly allocable to the taking of Lessee’s
Personal Property shall be the sole property of and payable to Lessee, and (b) if this Lease does
not terminate due to such taking or condemnation, Lessee shall be entitled to the award to the
extent required for restoration of the Leased Property, and Lessor shall be entitled to the balance
of the award not applied to restoration. In any condemnation proceedings, Lessor and Lessee shall
each seek their own award in conformity herewith, at their own expense. If this Lease does not
terminate due to a taking or condemnation, Lessee shall, with due diligence, restore the remaining
portion or portions of the Leased Property in the manner hereinabove provided. In such event, if
the proceeds of the award exceed Fifty Thousand Dollars ($50,000), then such proceeds shall be
deposited with a bank or financial institution designated by Lessor as if such award were casualty
insurance proceeds, and the amount so deposited will thereafter be treated in the same manner as
insurance proceeds are to be treated under Section 11.2 of this Lease until the restoration has been
completed and Lessee has been reimbursed for all the costs and expenses thereof. If the award is
insufficient to pay for the restoration, Lessee shall be responsible for the remaining cost and
expense of such restoration. Obligations to disburse any award shall be subject to (x) the collection
thereof, and (y) the release of such award by the Owner. In the event of a partial taking which
does not result in any termination of this Lease, the monthly Base Rent payable under Section 3.1
hereof shall not be reduced, unless such partial taking results in a loss of beds at the Facility, in
which event the Base Rent shall be reduced by a percentage equal to the percentage of beds at the
Facility lost as a result of such taking.

        12.4. No Abatement of Rent. This Lease shall remain in full force and effect and Lessee’s
obligation to make all payments of Rent and to pay all other Additional Rent as and when required
under this Lease shall, subject to the provisions of Section 12.3 above, remain unabated during the
Term notwithstanding any Condemnation involving the Leased Property.

        12.5. Waiver. The provisions of this Article shall be considered an express agreement
governing any Condemnation involving the Leased Property and, to the maximum extent permitted
by law, no local or State statute, law, rule, regulation or ordinance in effect during the Term which
provides for such abatement shall have any application in such case.

===== PAGE 424 =====
                                      ARTICLE 13.
                                 DEFAULTS AND REMEDIES

      13.1. Events of Default. The occurrence of any of the following acts or events shall be
deemed to be a default (“Event of Default”) on Lessee’s part:

               (a)      Lessee’s failure to pay within three (3) Business Days of when due any Rent
payment, or any part thereof, or any other sum or sums of money due or payable to Lessor under
the provisions of this Lease;

                (b)     Lessee’s failure to perform, or Lessee’s violation of, any of the covenants,
terms, conditions or provisions of this Lease, if such failure or violation shall not be cured within
thirty (30) days after written notice thereof by Lessor to Lessee, and if such default cannot be cured
within such thirty (30) day period, Lessees shall have an additional (30) day period to cure so long
as Lessee are diligently pursuing such cure to completion.

                (c)   The removal by any local, state or federal agency having jurisdiction over
the operation of the Facility of ten percent (10%) or more of the residents located at the Real
Property for a period of ten (10) days or more (unless such removal is the result of a casualty or
the exercise of eminent domain);

                (d)     Lessee’s failure to perform, or Lessee’s violation of, any of the terms,
conditions or provisions of the Master Lease, including, without limitation, any financial covenants
therein, or any Lessee requirements thereunder (except for those terms, conditions or provisions
requiring the making of any payments or which relate specifically to Lessor), if such failure or
violation shall not be cured within thirty (30) days (or such lesser time period as may be required
by the Master Lease) after notice thereof by Lessor to Lessee;

                (e)    Lessee’s removal of any physical beds, a substantial portion of the Personal
Property or Personal Property necessary to the operation of the Facility, not replaced within thirty
(30) days after written notice by Lessor to Lessee;

               (f)     Lessee’s sale or forfeiture of one or more of the licensed beds of the Facility;

               (g)     The making by Lessee of an assignment for the benefit of creditors;

                (h)    The levying of a writ of execution or attachment on or against Lessee’s
property which is not discharged or stayed by Lessee’s action contesting same, within sixty (60)
days after such levy or attachment or as to which Lessee has not deposited with Lessor an amount
equal to one hundred twenty five percent (125%) of the amount of such execution (provided if the
stay is vacated or ended, this section shall again apply);

               (i)     If proceedings are instituted in a court of competent jurisdiction for the
Lessee’s reorganization, liquidation or involuntary dissolution or for Lessee’s adjudication as
bankrupt or insolvent, or for the appointment of a receiver of Lessee’s property, and said

                                        ARTICLE 14.
                                     RIGHT TO CONTEST

         14.1. Right to Contest. Anything to the contrary stated herein notwithstanding, Lessee
shall have the right upon written notice thereof to Lessor, to contest by appropriate administrative
or legal proceedings, diligently conducted in good faith, the validity or application of any law,
ordinance, regulation or rule mentioned herein, and to delay compliance therewith pending the
prosecution of such proceedings, including any proceeding pursuant to Section 13 above. In the
event such contest involves a Substandard Quality of Care, Medicare or Medicaid decertification
or license revocation, Lessee shall give Lessor written notice of its election to contest same.
Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained herein, Lessee shall not be in default hereunder
for any administrative or legal proceeding that does not threaten Medicare or Medicaid
decertification or license revocation, provided, that during any contest: (a) no civil or criminal
liability would thereby be incurred by Lessor and no lien or charge would thereby be imposed
upon or satisfied out of the Real Property; (b) there continues during the course of such contest
authority to continue operations of the Real Property as a nursing home (which may be temporary
or provisional); (c) such situation does not cause Lessor to be in default pursuant to the terms of
any loan document; (d) Lessee demonstrates to the reasonable satisfaction of Lessor that Lessee
has a meritorious defense and has taken reasonable corrective action to address the circumstance,
event(s) or condition(s) giving rise to such actions; and (e) no criminal proceeding has been
brought against Lessee or any manager relating to the operation of the Leased Property or its
activities pursuant to this Lease or in connection with the Facility.

                                             25

===== PAGE 430 =====
         14.2. Non-Payment Default Extended Cure Period. Except for an Event of Default of
Lessee in the payment of Rent or any payment required hereunder, if for causes beyond Lessee’s
control it is not possible for Lessee to remedy the non-payment default within the time period
required, an Event of Default that arises solely under Section 13.1(b) and does not give rise to an
indemnity obligation that has not been timely performed by Lessee, then such Event of Default
shall not be deemed an Event of Default hereunder and Lessor shall not pursue any remedies
arising solely from the occurrence of such Event of Default for a period not to exceed sixty (60)
days after the initial cure period, if any, but only so long as all the following occur: (a) such
situation does not cause Lessor to be in default pursuant to the terms of the Master Lease, (b) no
civil or criminal liability would be incurred by Lessor or any person or entity affiliated with Lessor
as a result of the deferment, (c) no lien or charge would be imposed upon or satisfied out of all or
any part of the Leased Property as a result of the deferment; (d) Lessee continues to have the
authority to operate the Facility as a skilled care nursing home (which may be temporary or
provisional); (e) prior to the end of the cure period, or if none exists, then within three (3) business
days of receipt of written notice, Lessee gives Lessor notice of Lessee’s intention to institute all
steps necessary to remedy such situation, (f) Lessee shall, as soon as reasonably possible after
receipt of written notice, duly institute all steps necessary to remedy such situation, (g) Lessee
shall thereafter diligently prosecute to completion all steps necessary to remedy such situation, and
(h) Lessee shall remedy the situation during the period necessary to remedy such situation.

        14.3. Contest Right for Reduction in Beds. Lessee shall have the right to contest any
reduction in the number of licensed beds and shall notify Lessor within five (5) Business Days
following the date of such notice (or shorter period required to provide notice to Lessor not later
than ten (10) days prior to the cutoff date for any such contest) whether or not Lessee shall
undertake such contest. Any such contest by Lessee shall be conducted by counsel reasonably
satisfactory to Lessor and the cost of such contest shall be paid by Lessee. Lessor, at Lessor’s cost,
shall have the right to participate in any such contest by Lessee. If Lessee elects not to contest
such reduction, Lessor may, following written notice to Lessee of its intent to do so, contest any
such reduction. Any such contest by Lessor shall be conducted by counsel reasonably satisfactory
to Lessor and the cost of such contest shall be paid by Lessee. Lessor shall additionally have the
right to intervene in any such contest dealing with a reduction in the number of beds at the Facility.

no event, however, shall such holding over be deemed or construed to be or constitute a renewal
or extension of this Lease.

                                    ARTICLE 16.
                      LIABILITY OF LESSOR; INDEMNIFICATION

        16.1. Liability of Lessor. Lessor and its Affiliates shall not be liable to Lessee, its
employees, agents, invitees, licensees, customers, clients, residents and their respective family
members or guests for any damage, injury, loss, compensation or claim, including claims for the
interruption of or loss to Lessee’s business arising out of or resulting from any cause whatsoever
(other than a breach of Lessor’s obligations under this Lease or willful misconduct of Lessor, its
employees, agents, contractors or invitees), including: (a) repairs to any portion of the Leased
Property; (b) interruption in Lessee’s use of the Leased Property; (c) any accident or damage
resulting from the use or operation (by Lessor, Lessee or any other person or persons) of any
equipment within the Leased Property, including, heating, cooling, electrical or plumbing
equipment or apparatus; (d) the termination of this Lease by reason of the condemnation or
destruction of the Leased Property in accordance with the provisions of this Lease; (e) any fire,
robbery, theft or other casualty; and (f) the actions of any other person or persons. Any property
or personal effects stored or placed by the Lessee or its employees in or about the Leased Property
including Lessee’s Personal Property, shall be at the sole risk of the Lessee, unless the loss or
damage arises out of the gross negligence or willful misconduct of Lessor.

         16.2. Indemnification. In addition to and not in lieu of any other indemnity set forth
elsewhere herein, Lessee agrees to protect, indemnify and save harmless Lessor from and against
any claims, demands and causes of action asserted against or incurred by Lessor on account of:
(i) the operation of the Facility during the Term; (ii) any failure on the part of Lessee during the
Term of this Lease to perform or comply with any of the terms of this Lease; (iii) any breach by
Lessee of its representations, warranties or covenants hereunder; (iv) injury to or death of persons
or loss of or damage to property, occurring on the Real Property or any adjoining sidewalks, streets
or ways or in any manner growing out of or connected with the use or occupation of the Real
Property or the condition thereof, or the use of any existing or adjoining sewer system or any
adjoining sidewalks, streets or ways during the Term of this Lease; (v) civil monetary penalties
relating to activities during the Term; (vi) recapture due to an alleged overpayment or audit by
Medicaid or Medicare for services rendered during the Term; (vii) the underpayment of any tax by
Lessee with respect to operations during the Term, including amounts due for personal property or
bed taxes; (viii) any claim relating to the resident trust fund for the periods during the Term; and
(ix) in the event of the termination of this Lease, any recapture due to an alleged overpayment or
audit by Medicaid or Medicare for services rendered after the Commencement Date but prior to
such termination. Lessee further agrees to pay any reasonable attorneys’ fees and expenses
incident to the defense by Lessor of any such claims, demands or causes of action.
Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained in this Section 16.2(a), Lessee shall not have
any indemnity obligations hereunder to the extent that such indemnified liabilities claims, demands
or causes of action arise from the gross negligence, illegal acts, fraud or willful misconduct of
Lessor.

       16.3. Notice of Claim or Suit. Lessee shall promptly notify Lessor of any claim, action,
proceeding or suit instituted or threatened against Lessee of which Lessee receives written notice
or of which Lessee acquires actual knowledge which is not covered by insurance or likely to

earlier termination of this Lease.

                (b)     Within thirty (30) days of the end of each calendar month, Lessee shall
furnish to Lessor full and complete unaudited financial statements of Lessee and of the operation
of the Facility for such monthly period.

                 (c)    Lessee shall furnish to Lessor a copy of its cost report within ten (10) days
after filing thereof.

               (d)    Within thirty (30) days after Lessor’s written request therefor, Lessee shall
furnish to Lessor copies of all Financial Statements for the operation of the Facility received by
Lessee for the preceding month(s) and calendar quarter(s) in the then current calendar year to the
extent the same have not been previously provided to Lessors.

               (e)      Within forty-five (45) days after the date for filing Lessee’s tax return (as
the same may be extended), Lessee shall furnish Lessor with a copy of the tax return for the Facility
for said year, certified by an officer of Lessee to be true, correct and complete in all material
respects.

               (f)    Within thirty (30) days after the end of each month, Lessee shall furnish
Lessor with a copy of monthly census figures for the Facility with breakdowns of resident mix.

                (g)     In addition to the above financial statements, Lessee shall also provide to
Lessor such other financial statement(s) or information relating to its operation as may be
reasonably required under the Master Lease and which are consistent with industry standards. Any
such financial statement(s) or other information required by the terms of the Master Lease shall be
furnished to Lessor not later than five (5) days prior to the due date for Lessor to furnish the same
to Owner. Should the Master Lease require audited financial statements, Lessee shall furnish
audited financial statements. All financial information provided shall be prepared in accordance
with GAAP and shall be submitted electronically using the applicable template provided by Lessor
from time to time or, if no such template is provided by Lessor, in the form of unrestricted,
unlocked “.xls” spreadsheets created using Microsoft Excel (2003 or newer editions) or in such
other form as Lessor may reasonably require from time to time. If Lessee or any Guarantor
becomes subject to any reporting requirements of the Securities and Exchange Commission during
the Term, it shall concurrently deliver to Lessor such reports as are delivered pursuant to applicable
securities laws.

      18.3. Books and Records. At all times, Lessee shall keep and maintain in accordance
with GAAP records and books of account of Lessee’s operation in the Leased Property and records

and books of account of Lessee’s entire business operations in accordance with generally accepted

books of account covering Lessee’s entire business operations on the Leased Property, or as

        18.4. Quarterly Meetings. At Lessor’s request, Lessee shall make the Lessee’s property
management team and the executive officers of Lessee (or of Lessee’s general partner or managing

        18.6. Distributions. Following the occurrence of any Event of Default, Lessee shall not
(i) declare, pay or make any Distribution, (ii) apply any of its funds, property or assets to the
acquisition, redemption or other retirement of any membership or equity interest, (iii) otherwise
make any payments or Distributions to any stockholder, member, partner or other equity owner in
such person’s capacity as such, or (iv) make any payment of any management, consulting or
service fee to any related or affiliated party; and any obligation of Lessee to make any of the
foregoing payments shall be and hereby is made subordinate and junior in right of payment to the
payment of all Rent, and other payment obligations of Lessee hereunder. “Distribution” shall
mean any direct or indirect dividend, distribution or other payment of any kind or character
(whether in cash, securities or other property) in respect of any equity interests or any repayment
of indebtedness to any member of Lessee or any affiliate or relative thereof.

        18.7. Minimum Rent Coverage Ratio. Lessee shall maintain a Minimum Rent Coverage
Ratio (as defined below) of no less than 1.25 to 1. In the event that as of the applicable Testing
Date, the Minimum Rent Coverage Ratio for the applicable period of determination is less than
that required above, then an Event of Default shall not occur provided that: (a) no other Event of
Default shall have occurred and then be continuing, and (b) Lessee shall immediately deposit with
Lessor an amount equal to the amount equal to 6 monthly payments of then Base Rent (the
“Additional Deposit”). The Additional Deposit shall be held by Lessor as an additional security
deposit under this Lease and Lessor may, from time to time, without prejudice to any other right
or remedy, apply such Additional Deposit to the obligations due from Lessee under this Lease.
The Additional Deposit shall not be deemed an advance payment of Rent or a measure of Lessor’s
damages for any default under this Lease by Lessee, nor shall it be a bar or defense to any action
that Lessor may at any time commence against Lessee. The Additional Deposit shall be the
property of Lessor and it may commingle the Additional Deposit with other assets of Lessor, and

                                            31

===== PAGE 436 =====
Lessee shall not be entitled to any interest on the Additional Deposit. Provided that no Event of
Default then exists and is continuing, following the date on which Lessor determines that the
Minimum Rent Coverage Ratio for two (2) consecutive Testing Dates is greater than or equal to
the Minimum Rent Coverage Ratio, Lessor will cause the Additional Deposit to be returned to
Lessee. For purposes hereof, the term “Minimum Rent Coverage Ratio” means, as determined
on a Testing Date based on the applicable period of determination or measurement, the ratio of
(i) the Cash Flow (as defined below) for the Facility for the applicable period to (ii) Base Rent
payments relating to the Facility payable under this Lease for the applicable period. For purposes
hereof, the term “Testing Date” means, the date as of which the Minimum Rent Coverage Ratio
shall be determined for the applicable measurement period, which date shall be the last day of each
calendar quarter during the Term. Upon each Testing Date, the Minimum Rent Coverage Ratio
shall be determined based upon the six trailing calendar months ending on such Testing Date
(annualized for any such lesser period). For purposes hereof, the term “Cash Flow” means the
aggregate net income of Lessee attributable to the operation of the Facility as reflected on the
income statement of Lessee, plus (i) the provision for depreciation and amortization in such
income statement, plus (ii) the provision for management fees in such income statement, plus
(iii) the provision for income taxes in such income statement, plus (iv) the provision for Base Rent
payments and interest and lease payments, if any, relating to the Facility in such income statement,
plus (v) the provision for any other non-operating items in such income statement, and minus
(vi) an imputed management fee equal to six percent (6%) of gross revenues of the Facility (net of
contractual allowances).

      18.8. Minimum Occupancy. At all times during the Term, Lessees shall maintain a
minimum occupancy of each Facility and in the aggregate which is in no event less than the
minimum occupancy required under the Master Lease if applicable.

         18.9. Working Capital. At all times, Lessee shall maintain working capital in such an
amount (i) satisfactory to support continued licensure of the Facility and (ii) reasonably sufficient
to satisfy one hundred percent (100%) of Lessee’s short-term liabilities and payment obligations
for its long- term liabilities for the coming one hundred twenty (120) day period.

warranties in favor of Lessee with respect to the Leased Property; (g) all other assignable intangible
property not enumerated herein which is now or hereafter used in connection with the operation
of the Leased Property as a skilled nursing facility; and (h) the business of the Lessee as conducted
at the Leased Property as a going concern, including but not limited to the names of the business
conducted thereon and all telephone numbers presently in use therein and any proprietary materials
developed by Lessee and used in connection with its nursing home operations at locations other
than the Facility.

and deficiencies (including interest, penalties and reasonable attorney's fees, costs and expenses)
(hereinafter collectively “the Claims”) which either of them may suffer as a result of the breach
by Lessee in the performance of any of its commitments, covenants, or obligations under this
Article. Lessee does further agree to indemnify, defend and hold harmless Lessor, Lessor’s
Designee, and the successors and assigns of each of them, from any such Claims or with respect
to any suits, arbitration proceedings, administrative actions or investigations which relate to the
use by Lessee of the Leased Property prior to the Closing Date or any liability which may arise
from operation of the Leased Property as a skilled nursing facility prior to the Closing Date.
Lessor’s Designee shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Lessee from any Claims with respect
to any suits, arbitrations, proceedings, administrative actions or investigations which relate to the

Closing Date. The rights of Lessor under this paragraph are without prejudice to any other
remedies not inconsistent herewith which Lessor may have against Lessee pursuant to the terms
of this Lease.

        23.12 Anything to the contrary contained in this Article notwithstanding, in the event the
termination of this Lease is due to a default by Lessee, none of the provisions of this Article shall
in any way limit, reduce, restrict or modify the rights granted to Lessor pursuant to this Lease. If
the termination of this Lease is a result of an Event of Default, then to the extent any monies are
due to Lessee pursuant to this Article, such sums shall first be applied by Lessor to any damages
suffered by Lessor as a result of Lessee's Event of Default, with any excess remitted to Lessee
subject to the terms of this Article.

                                        ARTICLE 25.
                                      MISCELLANEOUS

        25.1. Limitation on Payment of Rent. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary
contained herein, all agreements between Lessor and Lessee herein are hereby expressly limited
so that in no event shall the Rent or any other amounts payable to Lessor under this Lease exceed
the maximum permissible under Applicable Laws.

       25.2. No Waiver. No release, discharge or waiver of any provision hereof shall be
enforceable against or binding upon Lessor or Lessee unless in writing and executed by Lessor or
Lessee, as the case may be. Neither the failure of Lessor or Lessee to insist upon a strict
performance of any of the terms, provisions, covenants, agreements and conditions hereof, nor the
acceptance of any Rent by Lessor with knowledge of a breach of this Lease by Lessee in the
performance of its obligations hereunder, or the following of any practice or custom at variance
with the terms hereof, shall be deemed or constitute a waiver of any rights or remedies that Lessor
or Lessee may have or a waiver of any subsequent breach or default in any of such terms,
provisions, covenants, agreements and conditions or the waiver of the right to demand exact
compliance with the terms hereof.

       25.3. Remedies Cumulative. Except as otherwise expressly provided by this Lease, to
the maximum extent permitted by law, each legal, equitable or contractual right, power and remedy

                                            45

===== PAGE 450 =====
of either party, now or hereafter provided either in this Lease or by statute or otherwise, shall be
cumulative and concurrent and shall be in addition to every other right, power and remedy and the
exercise or beginning of the exercise by such party of any one or more of such rights, powers and
remedies shall not preclude the simultaneous or subsequent exercise by such party of any or all of
such other rights, powers and remedies.

        25.4. Severability. Any clause, sentence, paragraph, section or provision of this Lease
held by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, illegal or ineffective shall not impair,
invalidate or nullify the remainder of this Lease, but rather the effect thereof shall be confined to
the particular clause, sentence, paragraph, section or provision so held to be invalid, illegal or

therein.

        25.5. Acceptance of Surrender. No surrender to Lessor of this Lease or of the Leased
Property shall be valid or effective unless agreed to and accepted in writing by Lessor and no act
by Lessor or any representative or agent of Lessor, other than such a written acceptance by Lessor,
shall constitute an acceptance of any such surrender.

        25.6. No Merger of Title. It is expressly acknowledged and agreed that it is the intent of
the parties that there shall be no merger of this Lease or of the leasehold estate created hereby by
reason of the fact that the same person may acquire, own or hold, directly or indirectly, this Lease
or the leasehold estate created hereby and the fee estate or ground Lessor’s interest in the Leased
Property.

        25.7. Quiet Enjoyment. Lessor covenants and agrees that so long as Lessee shall timely
pay all rents due to Lessor from Lessee hereunder and keep, observe and perform all covenants,
promises and agreements on Lessee’s part to be kept, observed and performed hereunder, Lessee
shall and may peacefully and quietly have, hold and occupy the Leased Property free of any
interference from Lessor or any person or entity claiming by, through or under Lessor; subject,
however, and nevertheless to the terms, provisions and conditions of this Lease, the Permitted
Encumbrances and documents affecting title to the Leased Property approved in writing by Lessee.

         25.8. Additional Rent. All payments to be made by the Lessee hereunder (other than
Base Rent), whether or not designated as “Additional Rent”, shall be deemed Additional Rent, so
that in the event of a default of payment when due, Lessor shall be entitled to all of the remedies
available at law or equity, or under this Lease, for the nonpayment of Rent.

                         OTHER REPORTING REQUIREMENTS

       In addition to other reports and notices required by the Lease, and without limiting or
amending any provision of the Lease requiring similar information to be provided by Lessee,
Lessee shall provide the following reports and information to Lessor as indicated as soon as
available, but in no event later than the time provided below:

      Regulatory Reports with respect to the Facility: Within ten (10) days after Lessee’s
       receipt, Lessee shall deliver to Lessor by written notice the following regulatory reports
       with respect to the Facility:

          o All federal, state and local licensing and reimbursement certification surveys,
            inspection and other reports received by Lessee as to the Facility and its
            operations, including state department of health licensing surveys and reports
            relating to complaint surveys;

          o All Medicare and Medicaid certification surveys;

          o All life safety code survey reports and/or fire marshal survey reports.

      Reports of Regulatory Violations: Within five (5) days after Lessee’s receipt of any of
       the following, Lessee shall deliver to Lessor by written notice copies of the same along
       with all related documentation:

          o Any survey or notice related in any way to a survey deficiency with a scope and
            severity of “G” or higher;

          o Any threat of denial of payment for new admissions, or any civil monetary
            penalty imposed in the amount of $500 per diem or more or $5,000 per incident or
            more;

          o Any violation of any federal, state, or local licensing or reimbursement
            certification statute or regulation, including Medicare or Medicaid;

          o Any suspension, termination or restriction (including immediate jeopardy) placed
            upon Lessee or any Facility, the operation of any Facility or the ability to admit
            residents or patients or any threat of any of the foregoing from state or federal
            authorities and/or agencies;

          o Any written threat of suspension or decertification of Lessee from State or federal
            healthcare programs;

          o The inclusion of any Facility on the “Special Focus List” maintained by CMS; or

===== PAGE 460 =====
           o Any written violation of any other permit, approval or certification in connection
             with any Facility or the operations thereof, by any federal, state or local authority,
             including Medicare or Medicaid;

      Annual Budgets: At least thirty (30) days prior to the commencement of each calendar
       year of Lessee during the Term, Lessee shall deliver to Lessor an annual operating budget
       covering the operations of each Facility for the forthcoming calendar year, which budget
       shall include month-to-month projections. Said annual operating budgets shall be in a
       form and shall contain such information as is reasonably acceptable to Lessor. Lessee
       shall promptly deliver to Lessor any subsequent revisions to annual operating budgets.
       Notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein, Lessor may require quarterly budgets in
       its sole discretion.

      Annual Capital Budgets. At least thirty (30) days prior to the commencement of each
       calendar year of Lessee during the Term, Lessee shall deliver to Lessor an annual budget
       setting forth Lessee’s reasonable estimate of the capital repairs, replacements, and
       improvements to each Facility that Lessee anticipates will be necessary in such calendar
       year to comply with its obligations under this Lease.

All financial reports required to be provided under this Lease shall be prepared in accordance with
GAAP, applied on a consistent basis, and certified by Lessee as being true and correct.
